issue.title: [RateLimiter] Fix SlidingWindowLimiter letting reservations through faster than the limit
issue.body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Branch?       | 6.4
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no
| Issues        | -
| License       | MIT

`SlidingWindowLimiter::reserve()` added every reservation to the hits of the current window, even when it acts in a later window. Once that window ended, the reserved hits counted as hits of the previous window and faded out, although they act in the new one. The wait was also always shorter than the end of the next window, however many tokens were reserved.

With a limit of 10 per minute, `consume(10)` at t=0 and ten `reserve(10)` at t=1 all acted between t=114 and t=119.4, and a `consume(10)` at t=119.9 was accepted too. Workers that call `consume()`, and `reserve()->wait()` when it is refused, like `Worker::rateLimit()` does for a transport with a `rate_limiter`, went over the limit: with 10 per minute, 5 workers got 15 hits per minute, 20 workers 30, and 50 workers 60.

The reserved hits beyond the size of a window are now carried to the next windows, like #64095 does for the fixed window, and a reservation waits for the first window that has room left. With the same workers, every minute now gets 10 hits, and no span of 60 seconds holds more than 10.

To know which window a hit acts in, the window keeps the limit it was counted with. It is stored as a second entry of the serialized state, and older versions only read the first one, so each version can read the states written by the other. The state also stays in the storage until its reserved hits have acted, like #63996 did for the token bucket.

When the limit changes, the hits are converted like `Window::configure()` does since #67087: full windows stay full and the last one is capped at the new limit, so lowering the limit doesn't turn hits that were already accepted into reservations. One difference with the current behavior: after `consume(50)` with a limit of 100 lowered to 10 and a 12 s window, the next hit was accepted once the 50 hits had faded, after 21.6 s, and it is now accepted at the end of the window, after 12 s. The other way around, with `consume(10)` and `reserve(10)` on a limit of 10 raised to 20, the next hit was accepted at once, and it now waits for the reserved window to fade, 18 s.

A state written before this fix with reservations in the next window is read as reservations over several windows, so after the upgrade the next reservation can wait longer once. It never lets more through.

Checks:
- The three new tests fail on 6.4 and pass with the fix. The RateLimiter tests pass. php-cs-fixer reports nothing.
- The new wait was checked on 200k random states, with limits up to 12, hit counts up to 5 times the limit and any number of tokens: the tokens are always free right after the wait and not right before.
- A state written by this branch is read by 6.4, and the other way around.

Not covered: when the reserved tokens do not divide the limit, a reservation can still be counted partly in one window and partly in the next, like with the fixed window, so a window can hold up to `limit + tokens - 1` hits. The average stays at the limit.

Merge-up to 7.4 and 8.1: no conflict. Merge-up to 8.2: no conflict either, but `getFullCapacityTime()`, used by `resetAt()`, assumes that the hits of the window fade out during the next one. With reservations, its `if ($this->hitCount)` branch needs to skip the windows they act in, otherwise the reset time is earlier than the retry time:

```php
$windows = $this->maxSize ? intdiv($this->hitCount - 1, $this->maxSize) : 0;
$hitCount = $this->hitCount - $windows * ($this->maxSize ?? 0);

return $this->windowEndAt + $this->intervalInSeconds * ($windows + 1 - 1 / $hitCount);
```

It can go in the merge-up, so that 8.2 never has the regression.

comment.body: Thanks for checking the numbers. The description now has the 18 s case next to the 21.6 s one, and says the `getFullCapacityTime()` change can go in the merge-up to 8.2.

issue.title: [Messenger] Fix RedisReceiver losing the rest of a batch when rejecting an entry without data fails
issue.body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Branch?       | 8.2
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no
| Issues        | -
| License       | MIT

Follow-up of #68020.

`RedisReceiver::get()` rejects the entries without data, for example the ones trimmed from the stream while they were pending. When that reject failed on a connection error, `get()` rethrew it right away. The other messages of the batch were already in flight in the connection, so the worker never got them, and since #66964 a worker with a `cooldown_strategy` keeps running, so they were not read again until it restarted.

`get()` now goes through the whole batch and returns its messages. The failure is thrown only when the batch has no message to return, as before. When `Connection::reject()` fails on a connection error, it now also drops the id from the messages in flight and reads the pending messages again from `'0'`, like #68020 does in `get()`. Otherwise the entry whose reject failed was not read again until a restart, and while it was the oldest pending entry of the group, the worker did not claim the messages that other consumers abandoned. With this PR that would also happen without a cooldown strategy, since the worker no longer stops on this failure.

Checks:
- The new receiver test and the new connection test fail on 8.2 and pass with the fix, and a second receiver test checks that the failure is still thrown when there is nothing else to return. The Redis bridge tests pass against Redis 7, with the cluster and sentinel ones skipped. php-cs-fixer reports nothing.

issue.title: [Scheduler] Fix cron triggers without a timezone taking the one of the last run after a restart
issue.body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Branch?       | 6.4
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no
| Issues        | -
| License       | MIT

When `MessageGenerator` builds its heap of triggers again, every trigger gets the time of the checkpoint. This happens when a worker with a stateful schedule restarts, `--time-limit` included, and when the schedule is changed at runtime. That date has the timezone of the run that came last. A cron expression without a timezone is computed in the timezone of the date it gets, as `CronExpressionTrigger` does on purpose since #50572, so it moved to the timezone of another task.

With the default timezone set to UTC, `cron('0 2 * * *')` next to `cron('0 9 * * *', timezone: 'America/New_York')`, both on a stateful schedule:

```
worker (re)started at 11-09 00:00 UTC
  ran at 11-09 02:00 UTC  nightly 02:00, no timezone   triggeredAt=11-09 02:00 UTC
  ran at 11-09 14:00 UTC  09:00 New York               triggeredAt=11-09 09:00 EST
worker (re)started at 11-10 00:00 UTC
  ran at 11-10 07:00 UTC  nightly 02:00, no timezone   triggeredAt=11-10 02:00 EST
```

From the first restart on, the nightly task ran at 07:00 UTC.

The time of the checkpoint is now converted to the timezone of the clock before it is given to the triggers. That is the timezone a new checkpoint starts with, so a restart computes the same dates as the first run. A task that already moved goes back to its slot on the first restart after the upgrade, so it can run twice that day or skip one day, like when its cron expression is edited.

Checks:
- The new test fails on 6.4 and passes with the fix. The Scheduler tests pass. php-cs-fixer reports nothing.
- With the same schedule over three days and a restart every day, the nightly task now runs at 02:00 UTC every day.

Merge-up to 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2: no conflict, the line is the same.

comment.body: Thanks for checking. I applied both suggestions in the test, and the description now says that a task that already moved goes back to its slot on the first restart after the upgrade.

issue.title: filter_retain_facts: retaining the document again puts the memories it re-tagged back on the document's tags
issue.body:
`filter_retain_facts` (#6400, on main, not in a release yet) can give a memory other tags than its document's when the memory is extracted. The next retain of the same document puts those memories back on the document's tags, and the hook never sees them again. On main `0bd5501`, with failing tests and a patch.

### What happens

1. An extension's `filter_retain_facts` returns `MemoryReview(tags=["hr"])` for facts about pay.
2. Retain `doc-pay` with `tags: ["public"]` and two chunks: "Alice's salary is ninety thousand euros, paid monthly." and a chunk about Bob's hiking. The salary memory is stored with `["hr"]`.
3. Retain `doc-pay` again: the same content (a client retry), `update_mode: "append"` with a new chunk, or an edit of the other chunk only.
4. The salary memory has the same id and `["public"]` again. A listing with `tags=["public"]` returns it, and consolidation builds a `public` observation from it.

The delta retain keeps the memories of unchanged chunks and doesn't extract them again, so the hook isn't asked about them. `update_memory_units_metadata_and_tags` (`retain/fact_storage.py`) then overwrites every survivor's tags with the document's tags plus its label tags, also when the document's tags didn't change. For a conversation integration that appends every turn, the hook's tags last until the next turn. The #6400 description says the memories of unchanged chunks are kept as they are, and the delta retain's own rule (#5630) is that an unchanged re-send writes nothing.

### Patch

Branch [`fix/review-tags-survive-relabel`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/tree/fix/review-tags-survive-relabel) in my fork, two commits on main `0bd5501`:

- [`00a7246`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/00a724694dd656a690ff966c758e811e3d85c5c4), tests only: `test_retaining_the_document_again_keeps_the_tags_the_extension_gave` in `tests/test_memory_review_hooks.py`, with the cases `same-content`, `one-chunk-edited` and `append`. It checks the unit ids too, so a re-extraction can't pass it. All three fail on main.
- [`aaf799b`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/aaf799b32ad8812b822de1fc5480a3f89424bcc5), the fix: the SQL delta path and the metadata-only path read the document's tags under the document lock before the upsert, and pass them as `previous_tags`. When the tag set is the same, a survivor keeps the tags it has. A retain that changes the document's tags still overwrites, as before.

Checks: the new tests pass with the fix, three runs in a row. Each of the two call sites has a case that fails without it. The neighbouring modules (delta retain, label tags, the partial tags PATCH, tag scope, append, observation invalidation and others) pass, except tests that need a real LLM key. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `ty` are clean. Postgres via pg0, hash embeddings instead of the local models.

Not covered:
- A document tags PATCH (`tags`, `add_tags` or `remove_tags`) still overwrites the hook's tags. Applying the tag change to each memory instead isn't safe without knowing what the hook decided: on a document whose items share one `document_id`, `remove_tags: ["b"]` would leave item B's memory with no tags, so readable by everyone, where main gives it `[a]`. Storing the review's tags per memory, or asking the hook again, would fix both paths. That's your call.
- The same goes for a retain that changes the document's tags.
- On a document whose items share one `document_id`, an identical re-send no longer merges the items' tags into each memory. Each memory keeps its own, which matches what a full replace gives.

issue.title: reembed: a re-run with another model of the same dimension keeps the first model's vectors
issue.body:
`hindsight-admin reembed` (#6372, on main, not in a release yet) tells a column left by an earlier run apart only by its dimension. Two cases on main `0bd5501`, with failing tests and a patch.

### 1. A stopped run, re-run with another model of the same size

`reembed_schema` drops a leftover `embedding_next` only when its dimension differs ("Left by an earlier run for a different model"). Models of the same size are common, including two of the defaults: `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` (local) and `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` (onnx) are both 384.

1. `reembed` with model B stops half way (Ctrl-C, a pod restart, a failed embedding call). Some rows already have B's vectors in `embedding_next`.
2. The operator switches to model C of the same dimension and runs `reembed` again. The help says "Resumable: re-run after an interruption and it continues".
3. The run keeps B's vectors, embeds only the rows that are still NULL, and swaps.

After the swap the table holds vectors from two models, and nothing says so. Recall embeds the query with C, so for the rows B wrote the similarity means nothing. `test_a_resumed_run_with_another_model_of_the_same_size_drops_the_first_models_vectors` stops a run after its first batch, and in a second case after the first mental model, then re-runs with another 8-dim model. On main the rows written before the stop keep the first model's vectors.

### 2. After the swap, a run with another model answers "already swapped"

Once the guard is installed, `reembed_schema` returns "already swapped" without checking which model the guard is for. If the operator changes the model before `--finish`, or runs the command from a shell that still has an old model set, nothing changes, while the CLI prints the new model and "Next: restart every server with the new model". Servers restarted on that model are refused by the guard (HS503) until `--finish`, and after it they write their vectors next to the old model's.

### Patch

Branch [`fix/reembed-resume-other-model`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/tree/fix/reembed-resume-other-model) in my fork, two commits on main `0bd5501`:

- [`c342c64`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/c342c64410d0595278703ea7e06ed02a5948bdba), tests only: three new cases in `tests/test_admin_reembed.py`. All three fail on main.
- [`9b3d30b`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/9b3d30b96e8d1a969c08f51f1b3ee44d67fe7d8f), the fix in `admin/reembed.py`:
  - `embedding_next` gets `embedding_model_id(...)` (provider, model, dimension) as its column comment. A leftover column with another model's comment is dropped, like one of another dimension.
  - The rename at the swap carries the comment to `embedding`. After the swap, a run with the same model still gets "already swapped". A run with another model is refused with both model names and a pointer to `--finish`. Re-embedding right away would replace the guard while servers may run either model, and a stale environment would quietly move the data back.
  - A swap made before this change has no comment and keeps the old answer.

Checks: the new tests pass with the fix, three runs in a row, and so do the existing reembed, rename-bank and HNSW index tests. Each new test fails with its half of the fix taken out (the check on `mental_models`, the refusal). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `ty` are clean. Postgres via pg0 locally; I didn't run the `test_57_reembed` system story.

Not covered:
- A run started before this change and resumed after it has no comment on `embedding_next`, so it starts over even with the same model. Safe, only slower.
- The model id leaves out settings that change the vectors without changing provider, model or dimension, such as `HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_PASSAGE_PREFIX`. A re-run that only changes the prefix still keeps the earlier vectors. The write guard compares the same id, so I left it as is.

issue.title: Option to count only incoming data in the heartbeat check (#1227)
issue.body:
Fixes #1227.

The missed-heartbeat check looks at `max(last_read, last_write)`, so a client that keeps sending its own heartbeats never notices that nothing comes back. That's the consumer from #1227 after the cable is pulled: it writes heartbeats into the kernel buffer and waits forever.

Checking `last_read` alone, as suggested in the issue, breaks clients that only publish: they never read, even though RabbitMQ keeps sending them heartbeats. So with the new option the check looks at incoming data, and if nothing was read, it looks without blocking whether data is waiting unread on the socket. A publisher keeps its connection that way.

```php
$config->enableIncomingHeartbeatCheck(true);
```

It's off by default because AMQProxy before 3.2.1 sent heartbeats only to a client that sent nothing (cloudamqp/amqproxy#254), so a publisher behind it would be disconnected. If you'd rather have it on by default, that's a one-line change.

The new tests use toxiproxy with a `timeout` toxic on `downstream`: nothing reaches the client, but its writes still go through. They cover a consumer that polls, the blocking `wait()` with `PCNTLHeartbeatSender` from the issue, the option being off, and a publisher that never reads. The publisher test fails if the check uses `last_read` alone. There are also unit tests for the decision logic and for `hasUnreadData()` on real socket pairs.

`SocketIO::read()` now updates `last_read` after each chunk, like `StreamIO`, so a big frame on a slow link doesn't look like a missed heartbeat.

comment.body:
Not special brokers, plain RabbitMQ.

By "silent broker" I mean that the TCP connection still looks open on the client, but nothing from the broker reaches it anymore. That happens when the network drops traffic without closing the connection: the unplugged cable in #1227, a firewall or NAT that forgot the connection, a load balancer that black-holes it. It also happens when the broker host is frozen while TCP stays up, like a paused VM or `docker pause`.

In all these cases the client's writes still succeed locally. On a cut network the kernel buffers them and keeps retransmitting for about 15 minutes by default (Linux `tcp_retries2`) before it gives up. So the client's own heartbeats keep `max(last_read, last_write)` fresh, and `AMQPHeartbeatMissedException` is never thrown. The consumer from #1227 waits forever.

The new test reproduces it with toxiproxy: a `timeout` toxic on `downstream` drops everything coming from RabbitMQ, while the client's writes still reach it.

Why it's opt-in: RabbitMQ sends heartbeats whenever it has nothing else to send, even to a client that only publishes, so the check is safe with it. But AMQProxy before 3.2.1 sent heartbeats only to a client that sent nothing, and a publisher behind it would be disconnected. I didn't want to break that setup by default.

discussion.title: hindsight-php: a PHP client, and memory for Laravel AI SDK agents
discussion.body:
I use Hindsight as memory for my coding agents and work mostly in PHP. There was no PHP client, so I wrote one: [hindsight-php](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight-php).

It has two parts.

**A plain PHP client.** Retain, recall, reflect, banks and their config, documents, directives, mental models and operations. Method names follow the Python and TypeScript clients. If the server ignores a parameter, the `X-Ignored-Params` header becomes a PSR-3 warning, so a typo doesn't silently change results.

**Memory for Laravel AI SDK agents.** One middleware: before the agent answers, it recalls what the bank knows about the user; after it answers, it retains the exchange.

```php
public function middleware(): array
{
    return [Memory::bank("user-{$this->user->id}")->queue()];
}
```

With `->queue()`, the retain runs as a queued job and retries while the API is down. Every attempt sends the same `operation_id`, so a retry after a lost response doesn't store the memory twice. I checked that on real 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 servers: the same retain twice without an ID gives two copies, with an ID one.

`Hindsight::fake()` lets you test agents without a server. CI compares its tag filters and rejected requests with real servers.

v0.3.0 also ships a Laravel Boost guideline and agent skill, which `php artisan boost:install` offers.

It isn't on Packagist yet, so install from GitHub:

```bash
composer config repositories.hindsight-php vcs https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight-php
composer require fedoseev/hindsight-php:^0.3
```

It's a community package, MIT, not affiliated with Vectorize. If you run Hindsight from PHP, I'd like to hear what's missing.

issue.title: Whole-bank restore: a crash-retry can delete a bank that took the target id, and refusals are retried before failing
issue.body:
The two follow-ups #6408 lists under "Not changed", with failing tests and a patch.

### 1. A crash-retried restore can delete a bank that took the target id

The crash-retry marker records only `restored_bank_id`. On retry, `import_bank_async` deletes the target bank when the marker names it and a bank with that id exists.

1. A restore into `dst` commits its bank row and the marker, then the worker dies mid-import.
2. Before the retry runs, someone deletes the half-restored `dst`, and a new bank `dst` appears (a retain into `dst`, a bank create, another restore).
3. The retry finds the marker and a bank called `dst`, deletes it as its own leftovers, and restores the archive.

The new bank's data is gone. On main `0bd5501`, `test_a_retry_leaves_alone_a_bank_that_took_the_id_after_the_crash` shows it: the crash is injected after the first document batch, as in `test_import_bank_retried_after_a_crash_starts_over`, and after the retry the bank holds `['doc-1', 'doc-2']` from the archive instead of the new bank's `['dave']`.

The window needs a crash, a manual delete and a recreate before the retry, so it is narrow. The cost is a deleted bank that the operation never created.

### 2. Restore refusals are retried before the operation fails

`_restore_bank` refuses with a plain `ValueError` when the target exists, when another restore created it first (#6408), and when the archive asks for the bank config but has no bank row. A rerun refuses the same way, but `_is_non_retryable_task_error` does not know these errors, so the worker retries them (`worker_max_retries`, default 3 × 60 s) before marking the operation failed. A clone exports the source bank again on each of those runs.

### Patch

Branch [`fix/restore-refusals-and-retry-marker`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/tree/fix/restore-refusals-and-retry-marker) in my fork, two commits on main `0bd5501`:

- [`1edffad`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/1edffad57154cb050d4fdce6898ee25e67324185), tests only: `tests/test_bank_restore_retry.py`, plus a classification assertion in the two refusal tests of `tests/test_bank_restore_race.py`. On main 6 of the 7 fail: the id-taken retry (with and without the bank config), and the classification of all three refusals. The seventh guards existing behaviour and passes on both: a marker without the new field still lets the retry start over.
- [`1f941ed`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/1f941ed296762aaa27c3bcd2e0e7a66691686480), the fix:
  - `on_bank_created` also records `restored_bank_internal_id`, read in the same transaction after the restore has checked the row is its own. The retry deletes the bank only if it still has that `internal_id`. A marker without the field, from an operation that crashed before the upgrade, keeps the id-only behaviour.
  - The three refusals raise `BankRestoreRefusedError(ValueError)`, which `_is_non_retryable_task_error` treats as deterministic. It is still a `ValueError`, so the HTTP layer's `except ValueError` and the tests that expect one are unchanged. The stored `error_message` now starts with `BankRestoreRefusedError:` instead of `ValueError:`.

Checks: the new and existing restore tests pass with the fix. So do the transfer, admin transfer and backup, streaming import, file storage, operation status and retry-classification suites (176 tests), and the new tests passed three repeated runs in parallel. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean. I ran them locally with ONNX embeddings instead of torch, and not on Oracle; for Oracle I only read the code (`internal_id` comes back as a UUID there too, per #6408, and is compared as a string).

Not covered:
- The alias refusal inside the restore (`refuse_alias_as_bank_id_on_conn`, `OperationValidationError` 409) and `validate_new_bank_id` are deterministic too, but they stay retried. They are shared with the HTTP path, so I left them alone.
- The fix narrows the window rather than closing it. The `internal_id` check and `delete_bank` are separate statements, and the delete goes by bank id, so a bank swapped in between them would still be deleted.

issue.title: Two concurrent retains of the same document with the same content store its facts twice
issue.body:
### Bug Description

**Two retains of the same content for the same document, running at once, store the facts of a multi-batch document twice.** This is what a client retrying a slow retain produces, or a retain task run again while its first run is still writing.

The streaming write serializes same-document writers with `lock_document_for_write` and detects a concurrent request by comparing the document row's `content_hash` with its own ("Later batches: verify we still own the document" in `orchestrator.py`). Two requests with the same content have the same hash, so the check passes for both:

1. A writes batch 1.
2. B's first batch runs `handle_document_tracking`, deletes A's data and writes its own batch 1.
3. A's batch 2 finds the hash unchanged and writes; B's batch 2 does the same, and so on.

Every batch after the first is written by both. Chunks are deduplicated by their deterministic ids, facts are not. With the default `retain_chunk_batch_size` of 100 this needs a document of more than 100 chunks, which is also the kind of document whose extraction runs long enough for a client to retry.

### Steps to Reproduce

A fresh local server from current `main` with `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`, and small chunks and batches so that a short document spans several batches:

```bash
HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE=300 HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_CHUNK_BATCH_SIZE=2 hindsight-api
```

```python
import asyncio, httpx

B = "http://localhost:8888/v1/default/banks"
DOC = " ".join(f"Fact number {i}: project Orion milestone {i} was reviewed by team {chr(65 + i % 26)} on day {i}." for i in range(60))

async def retain(c, bank):
    r = await c.post(f"{B}/{bank}/memories", json={"items": [{"content": DOC, "document_id": "doc"}], "async": False}, timeout=600)
    r.raise_for_status()

async def main():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as c:
        await retain(c, "once")
        await asyncio.gather(retain(c, "twice"), retain(c, "twice"))

asyncio.run(main())
```

```sql
SELECT bank_id, count(*), count(DISTINCT text) FROM memory_units WHERE bank_id IN ('once', 'twice') GROUP BY 1;
-- once  | 20 | 20
-- twice | 38 | 20
```

Recall on `twice` returns 38 results, 18 of them the same text twice; `chunks` and `documents` hold 20 and 1 for both banks. 38 = the 2 facts of batch 1, written once, plus the 18 of batches 2–10, written twice.

### Expected Behavior

The document's facts are stored once, whichever request finishes it.

### Actual Behavior

Every fact outside the first batch is stored twice, and recall, consolidation and everything else that reads the bank see the duplicates.

### Version

`main` at 1a37e009c (reproduced). v1.2.0 has the same check (checked in the source, not run).

### LLM Provider

None for the reproduction (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`). The race does not depend on the provider; a real LLM only makes the window longer.

### Where else

A second retain that starts after the first has already committed a batch takes a different route and duplicates the same way. A document within `retain_batch_tokens` goes through `_try_delta_retain`, whose only write gate is `current_hash != doc_hash_at_load`; a split document takes the recovery path, which skips the chunks committed at probe time and then writes the rest alongside the first retain. Both reproduced in the test suite.

### A failing test

[f5be73d](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/f5be73d48) on [`repro/concurrent-same-content-retain`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commits/repro/concurrent-same-content-retain) adds `test_concurrent_retains_of_the_same_content_store_each_fact_once` to `tests/test_delta_retain_duplicates.py`: a 24-chunk document retained twice at once with two chunks per batch, checking that every chunk ends up with exactly one fact. It fails on `main` with duplicate memory units, 3 runs out of 3.

### What does not fix it

I tried the obvious fix first and it is wrong, so it is not in the branch: under the document lock, abort the remaining batches (as after a detected takeover) when a batch finds its chunks already stored by id and chunk hash. It passes the test above, but only because the chunks finish extracting in index order there. Batches are built in extraction-completion order, so with a real LLM the two runs hold different chunks in each batch. Each then hits an overlap at a different point, both abort, and the document is left with gaps while both calls report success. With random per-chunk delays that happened in about 10 of 24 runs, keeping 6 to 16 of 20 chunks.

What looks right instead: under the lock, skip the chunks (and their facts) that the other run has already stored and write the rest of the batch, so whichever run gets to a chunk first writes it and the document always ends complete. The catch is that phase-1 entity resolution runs before the lock and is indexed by fact position, so the batch would need to be filtered before phase 1 and checked again under the lock. The delta write in `_run_delta_db_work` would need the same check after `lock_document_hash`.

issue.title: Two whole-bank restores into the same new bank id merge and duplicate every fact; bank export/import archives outlive their bank
issue.body:
### Bug Description

**Two whole-bank restores into the same new bank id both succeed and merge, so every fact ends up in the bank twice.** "A bank restore writes into a fresh bank (it is not a merge)" holds for one restore at a time, but not for two that overlap: a client that retries an upload after a timeout, a double submit, or two `/clone` calls with the same `target_bank_id`.

Both restores pass the existence checks: the one at submission, because the target does not exist yet, and the `SELECT 1 FROM banks` inside the restore transaction, because neither has committed. The second one's bank row insert (`_restore_rows` for the `banks` table, i.e. `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, or `create_bank_row_on_conn` without the config component, whose return value the restore ignores) then waits for the first transaction, inserts nothing, and the restore carries on writing its documents and facts into the bank the first one created. Documents and chunks are deduplicated by their keys, facts are not.

A smaller one in the same area: **the whole-bank export and import archives are stored outside the bank's storage prefix**, so deleting the bank leaves them behind. `_handle_export_bank` and `submit_bank_import_async` build `banks/{bank_id}/exports|imports/...` keys, while the document export and import use `bank_storage_prefix(bank_id)` (`tenants/{schema}/banks/{bank_id}/...`), and `delete_bank` deletes only that prefix. The comment there says "A deleted bank takes its whole prefix (exports and imports included)". These keys also miss the tenant segment that every other file of the bank carries.

### Steps to Reproduce

On a fresh local server (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`, current `main`, default `native` file storage):

```bash
B=http://localhost:8888/v1/default/banks
J='Content-Type: application/json'

curl -s -X POST "$B/src/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Source bank note.","document_id":"d1"}]}'
curl -s -X POST "$B/src/transfer/export" -H "$J" -d '{}'      # operation id; its result_metadata.storage_key once completed
curl -s -o export.zip "http://localhost:8888/v1/default/files/download/<storage_key>"

# The same archive restored twice into the same new bank, e.g. an upload retried by the client:
curl -s -X POST "$B/src/transfer/import?target_bank_id=dst" -F "file=@export.zip;type=application/zip"
curl -s -X POST "$B/src/transfer/import?target_bank_id=dst" -F "file=@export.zip;type=application/zip"

curl -s "$B/src/operations"                                     # both import_bank operations: completed
curl -s -X POST "$B/dst/memories/recall" -H "$J" -d '{"query":"Source bank note"}'   # the fact comes back twice
```

`SELECT count(*) FROM memory_units WHERE bank_id = 'dst'` gives 2 for the 1 fact of `src`; `documents` and `chunks` give 1. The worker picked both tasks up at once and logged `Imported bank dst ... 1 doc(s), 1 fact(s)` twice.

The archives:

```bash
curl -s -X DELETE "$B/src"
# SELECT storage_key FROM file_storage WHERE storage_key LIKE 'banks/src/%';
# -> banks/src/exports/<uuid>/transfer.zip is still there
```

### Expected Behavior

One restore creates the bank; the other fails and writes nothing. The archives of a bank go when the bank does.

### Actual Behavior

Both operations complete and `dst` holds every fact twice. The export archive stays in file storage after its bank is deleted. So would an uploaded import archive whose restore did not complete: `_handle_import_bank` deletes it only after a successful restore (read in the code).

### Version

`main` at 1a37e009c (reproduced). v1.2.0 has the same code paths (checked in the source, not run).

### LLM Provider

None (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`); not LLM-related.

### Patch

A fix with tests is in my fork, as two commits on [`fix/concurrent-restore-and-transfer-archive-keys`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commits/fix/concurrent-restore-and-transfer-archive-keys): [d807683](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/d80768303) (the race) and [77871cf](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/77871cf25) (the archive keys).

- The restore mints the restored bank row's `internal_id` in Python, the way `create_bank_row_on_conn` already does, instead of leaving it to the column default, and checks after the insert that the row is its own. Without the config component it checks `create_bank_row_on_conn`'s return. Either way the losing restore raises "Target bank 'dst' was created by another restore while this one ran; nothing was restored" and its transaction rolls back. Its own message, because the usual "Delete the bank first" would point at the other restore's bank. An archive whose bank config has no bank row now gets a plain error instead of a foreign key violation further down.
- The refusal comes before `on_bank_created`, so the losing operation no longer records `restored_bank_id` for a bank it did not create. Today, if the worker crashed during the losing restore, the retry would delete the winner's bank as its own half-restored one.
- `_handle_export_bank` and `submit_bank_import_async` build their keys under `bank_storage_prefix(bank_id)`, like the document export and import. The download endpoint and `retrieve_bank_file_stream` already accept that layout. Archives already stored under the old keys are not moved and are still left behind when their bank is deleted; sweeping `banks/{bank_id}/` by prefix is not safe, since that prefix is shared across tenants.

Tests: `tests/test_bank_restore_race.py` holds the first restore's transaction open in `on_bank_created` until a second restore of the same archive is blocked on it (`pg_blocking_pids`), with and without the config component; both cases fail on `main` (the second restore does not raise and the target ends up with twice the facts) and pass with the patch. Two tests in `tests/test_bank_file_storage.py` run a real bank export and delete the bank, and check where the import stashes its archive; both fail on `main`. The existing `test_deleting_a_bank_deletes_everything_under_its_prefix` passed on `main` because it builds its export key under the prefix by hand. `test_bank_aliases`, `test_document_transfer`, `test_admin_bank_transfer`, `test_transfer_streaming_import`, `test_repair_bank_vector_indexes`, `test_streaming_file_storage`, `test_admin_rename_bank`, `test_delete_bank_leaves_no_rows` and the new files pass (219 tests); ruff is clean.

Not changed, possible follow-ups:
- The refused restore is a `ValueError` raised inside the task, which `_is_non_retryable_task_error` does not treat as deterministic, so it is retried before the operation fails, like the existing "already exists" check and the alias refusal mentioned in #6280.
- The crash-retry marker stores only the bank id. If a retry deletes its half-restored bank and another restore creates a bank under that id before the next attempt, that attempt is now refused, and the one after it would find the marker and delete the other restore's bank. Storing the minted `internal_id` in the marker and deleting only on a match would close it. Narrow, and it was a silent merge before.

issue.title: Bank aliases can be taken over: clone, transfer import and rename-bank into an alias name; deleted bank's aliases stay cached
issue.body:
### Bug Description

Clone and transfer import into a target id that is already an **alias** of another bank succeed. They create a real bank under that name, and since alias resolution prefers a real bank, the alias silently stops reaching the bank it names: every caller still using it now reads from and writes to the copy.

The docs promise the opposite: "A name is unique across banks and aliases ... so an alias can never reach two banks". The create path already enforces it (`create_bank_row_on_conn` refuses an alias with `409`, pinned by `test_a_bank_cannot_be_created_under_an_alias`). The restore does not go through that path when the bank-config component is included, which is the default for both `/clone` and `/transfer/import`: `import_bank` writes the archived `banks` row itself via `_restore_rows`, and `submit_bank_clone_async` / `submit_bank_import_async` only check that the target is not an existing bank. With `include_bank_config=false` the restore does call `create_bank_row_on_conn` and the clone is refused.

The admin CLI `rename-bank --to <alias>` has the same gap: `_rename_bank` checks `banks` for the new id but not `bank_aliases`.

This hits exactly the migration the aliases page describes: clients are moving to the new id in phases, and anyone cloning or restoring a bank under that id redirects them without an error.

A smaller one in the same area: **deleting a bank does not drop its aliases from the resolver cache.** `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes the rows and `delete_alias` invalidates its entry, but `delete_bank` invalidates nothing for the aliases. After any request has routed through an alias, a write to that name within `HINDSIGHT_API_BANK_ALIAS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` (10 s by default) on the same process goes to the deleted id and recreates the deleted bank, instead of creating a bank under the freed name. The docs say "Deleting a bank removes its aliases, freeing those names for reuse".

### Steps to Reproduce

On a fresh local server (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`, current `main`):

```bash
B=http://localhost:8888/v1/default/banks
J='Content-Type: application/json'

curl -s -X POST "$B/orig/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Original bank note.","document_id":"orig-doc"}]}'
curl -s -X POST "$B/src/memories"  -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Source bank note.","document_id":"src-doc"}]}'
curl -s -X POST "$B/orig/aliases"  -H "$J" -d '{"alias":"next"}'

curl -s "$B/next/documents"                     # orig-doc: the alias reaches orig
curl -s -X POST "$B/src/clone?target_bank_id=next"   # 202; give the operation a second
curl -s "$B/next/documents"                     # src-doc: the alias now reaches the clone
curl -s "$B/orig/aliases"                       # orig still lists "next"
curl -s -X POST "$B/next/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Meant for orig.","document_id":"via-alias"}]}'
curl -s "$B/orig/documents"                     # via-alias is not here; it went into the clone
```

`POST $B/src/transfer/import?target_bank_id=<alias>` with an archive from `/transfer/export` behaves the same.

The cache one:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$B/old/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Old bank note."}]}'
curl -s -X POST "$B/old/aliases"  -H "$J" -d '{"alias":"reuse"}'
curl -s "$B/reuse/aliases"        # routes to old, and caches it
curl -s -X DELETE "$B/old"
curl -s -X POST "$B/reuse/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"For the freed name."}]}'
# answers "bank_id": "old": the deleted bank is back, and no bank "reuse" exists
```

### Expected Behavior

`409` at submission, as for creating a bank under an alias directly, and the alias keeps reaching its bank. Same for `rename-bank`.

After a bank is deleted, its former alias names are free at once on the process that deleted it.

### Actual Behavior

`202`, the operation completes, a real bank named like the alias exists, and the alias routes to it. The original bank keeps listing the alias, which is now dead.

For the cache case, the deleted bank is recreated under its old id with the new write in it.

### Version

`main` at 32dbd7e (reproduced). 1.1.0 has the same code paths (checked in the source, not run).

### LLM Provider

None (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`); not LLM-related.

### Patch

A fix with tests is in my fork, as two commits on [`fix/restore-under-alias`](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commits/fix/restore-under-alias): [b8fbdf2](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/b8fbdf2) (the takeover) and [1f1a2c4](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/1f1a2c4) (the cache).

- `bank_utils.refuse_alias_as_bank_id_on_conn`: the existing check from `create_bank_row_on_conn`, moved into a helper.
- `import_bank` calls it inside the restore transaction, next to the "target already exists" check, so the config path is covered too (this also covers the admin CLI restore).
- `submit_bank_clone_async` and `submit_bank_import_async` call it up front, so the caller gets `409` instead of a failed operation.
- `_rename_bank` refuses another bank's alias and names that bank. Renaming onto the bank's *own* alias (the end of the migration the admin docs suggest aliases for) drops that alias in the same transaction; today it leaves a `(new, new)` self-alias row, which the API otherwise forbids.
- `delete_bank` reads the bank's aliases before the row goes and invalidates them after commit, like `delete_alias` does.
- One line in the aliases docs says clone, transfer import and `rename-bank` are covered.

Tests: clone and transfer import over HTTP answer `409` and create no bank; `import_bank_async` refuses with and without the config component; rename refuses another bank's alias and moves nothing; rename onto its own alias leaves only the other aliases; a write to a deleted bank's former alias creates the new bank. Six of the new cases fail on `main` (the restore without the config component already passed) and all pass with the patch. `test_bank_aliases`, `test_admin_rename_bank`, `test_document_transfer`, `test_admin_bank_transfer`, `test_bank_utils`, `test_delete_bank_leaves_no_rows` and the transfer import suites pass (138 tests); ruff is clean.

Side note, not changed: a refusal raised inside the background restore (an `OperationValidationError` 409, like the existing "already exists" `ValueError`) is retried three times before the operation fails, because only 401/403 count as non-retryable; a clone re-exports the source on every attempt. With the check at submission this only matters for races.

issue.title: Malformed input answers 500 instead of 4xx: non-UUID directive ids, out-of-range directive priority, NUL bytes outside retain
issue.body:
### Bug Description

Several requests with ordinary client mistakes reach Postgres and come back as `500`, while the same kind of mistake elsewhere in the API already gets a `4xx`. A client, or an SDK that retries on 5xx, cannot tell them apart from a server fault.

I sent edge-case requests to a fresh local server (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`). 10 of 130 answered `500`, in three groups:

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET` / `PATCH` / `DELETE /directives/not-a-uuid` | `500 invalid input for query argument $2: 'not-a-uuid' (invalid UUID ...)` |
| `DELETE /memories/not-a-uuid/observations` | `500 badly formed hexadecimal UUID string` |
| `POST /directives` with `"priority": 2147483648` | `500 ... value out of int32 range` |
| NUL byte (`\u0000`) in a recall `tags` filter | `500 Failed to search memories (CharacterNotInRepertoireError)` |
| NUL byte in `GET /memories/list?q=` | `500 invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00` |
| NUL byte in a document id (`GET /documents/a%00b`) | same |
| NUL byte in a directive name or content | same |
| NUL byte in a bank `name` (`PUT /banks/{id}`) | same |

For comparison, `GET /memories/not-a-uuid` already answers `400 Invalid memory_id: 'not-a-uuid' is not a valid UUID` (#3062), and retain scrubs NUL bytes (#3908, #3921).

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
pip install "hindsight-api-slim[local-onnx,embedded-db]==1.1.0"
HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=onnx HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_PROVIDER=rrf hindsight-api

B=http://localhost:8888/v1/default/banks/demo
J='Content-Type: application/json'
curl -s -X POST "$B/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Alice works at Google."}]}'

curl -s "$B/directives/not-a-uuid"
curl -s -X DELETE "$B/memories/not-a-uuid/observations"
curl -s -X POST "$B/directives" -H "$J" -d '{"name":"n","content":"c","priority":2147483648}'
curl -s -X POST "$B/memories/recall" -H "$J" -d '{"query":"alice","tags":["a\u0000"]}'
curl -s "$B/memories/list?q=a%00b"
```

### Expected Behavior

A `4xx` that names the problem, like the routes that already validate their input.

### Actual Behavior

`500`, with the database error as the detail, and an `ERROR` traceback in the server log for each request.

### Where it happens (main @ dd250e6)

- `MemoryEngine.get_directive`, `update_directive` and `delete_directive` pass `directive_id` straight to the query. `clear_observations_for_memory` calls `uuid.UUID(memory_id)` inside the transaction. None of the four routes catch `ValueError`.
- `CreateDirectiveRequest.priority` and `UpdateDirectiveRequest.priority` are unbounded `int`, but `directives.priority` is `INT`.
- `_internal_error`, and the recall, retain and reflect-tool catch-alls, map every database error to `500`, including SQLSTATE `22021` (character_not_in_repertoire) and `22P05` (untranslatable_character). On these routes that text always comes from the client.

### Patch

CONTRIBUTING says external PRs are closed, so the fix is on a fork branch you can cherry-pick or rewrite: https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/bea0cb7883c4b901b552108b65975914eced81dc (6 files, +328/−4)

- The four routes raise and map the same `Invalid ...: '...' is not a valid UUID` `ValueError` to `400`, like #3062, and pass the canonical id on. Otherwise `{...}` and `urn:uuid:...` spellings, which `uuid.UUID` accepts and the uuid column rejects, would still 500; now they get the usual `404`.
- A shared `check_directive_priority()` runs as a field validator on the two request models and on `BankTemplateDirective`, and in `create_directive` / `update_directive` for the MCP tools. A template import with an out-of-range priority now fails before it writes anything. I used validators instead of `ge`/`le` so the OpenAPI and bank-template schemas, and the generated clients, stay unchanged.
- A small `_unstorable_text()` helper walks the cause chain like `_store_unavailable()` and maps those two SQLSTATEs to `400`. `_internal_error` and the three custom catch-alls use it.
- Tests: stub-engine tests for the id checks and canonical forms (same pattern as `test_get_entity_uuid_validation.py`), priority tests for the models and the engine, `_internal_error` tests, and a structural test that every catch-all calling `_store_unavailable` by hand also calls `_unstorable_text`. The new tests fail on `dd250e6`.

Not covered: a lone surrogate (`\ud800`) in the same fields still answers `500`, because asyncpg fails to encode it before the query is sent. That probably needs a separate decision on where to reject it.

With the patch, the same 130 requests produce no `5xx`. `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

### Version

1.1.0 (`hindsight-api-slim` from PyPI), and main @ dd250e6

### LLM Provider

None (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`); not involved.

comment.body:
Update: the branch now also covers the lone-surrogate case I listed as not covered: https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/c2aa3ac521889c63fd26f93d729c56e168e7feeb

asyncpg fails to encode `"\ud800"` before the query is sent, so the chain holds `DataError` ← `UnicodeEncodeError("surrogates not allowed")` and no SQLSTATE. `_unstorable_text` now recognises that `UnicodeEncodeError`; any other `UnicodeEncodeError` stays a `500`. A directive name, a bank name or a recall tag with `\ud800` now answers `400`.

Still `500`: a lone surrogate in a value stored as jsonb (bank config, a mental model trigger). Postgres rejects it with `22P02`, which also covers real server errors, so I didn't map it.

The first commit was also revised after review: canonical UUIDs (`{...}` and `urn:uuid:...` now get the usual `404`), and the priority check moved to validators plus the engine, so template import and the MCP tools are covered and the OpenAPI document is unchanged. The issue text above links the current commit.

A separate bug found the same way: #6235 (mental model ids).

issue.title: Mental model ids are not validated: an id with "/" becomes unreachable over HTTP and breaks bank export; knowledge page max_tokens overflows
issue.body:
### Bug Description

`CreateMentalModelRequest` documents `id` as "alphanumeric lowercase with hyphens" but doesn't enforce it. `BankTemplateMentalModel` does. Two consequences:

1. **An id with `/` can't be read or deleted through the HTTP API afterwards.** `POST /mental-models` stores it, but the slash splits the URL path, so `GET` and `DELETE /mental-models/{id}` answer `404` whether it is sent raw or as `%2F`. Only the MCP tools, which take the id as an argument, can still reach it.
2. **Any non-conforming id breaks `GET /banks/{bank_id}/export` for the whole bank.** Export validates every mental model against `BankTemplateMentalModel` and answers `500` (`Mental model id '...' must be alphanumeric lowercase with hyphens`) until the model is deleted, which for a `/` id means going through MCP.

A related gap: knowledge pages are mental models, but `CreatePageRequest.max_tokens` and `UpdateNodeRequest.max_tokens` are unbounded. A large value overflows the `INT` column with a `500` (`value out of int32 range`). Mental models themselves are bounded to 256..8192.

### Steps to Reproduce

I reproduced this on a local server with `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`. There the create call answers `500` for the missing LLM, but the row is stored anyway (see the note at the end). Nothing on the id path depends on the provider, so with an LLM configured the same id should be stored without any error.

```bash
B=http://localhost:8888/v1/default/banks/demo
J='Content-Type: application/json'
curl -s -X POST "$B/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Alice works at Google."}]}'

curl -s -X POST "$B/mental-models" -H "$J" -d '{"id":"team/standup","name":"Standup","source_query":"What did the team decide?"}'
curl -s "$B/mental-models?detail=metadata"            # lists "team/standup"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$B/mental-models/team%2Fstandup"            # 404
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$B/mental-models/team%2Fstandup"  # 404
curl -s "$B/export"                                   # 500

curl -s -X POST "$B/knowledge-base/pages" -H "$J" -d '{"name":"P","source_query":"q","max_tokens":1099511627776}'  # 500
```

### Expected Behavior

`422` for an id outside the documented form and for `max_tokens` outside 256..8192, so every stored model stays reachable and exportable.

### Actual Behavior

The id is stored; the model becomes unreachable (with `/`) and the bank's export answers `500`. The large `max_tokens` answers `500`.

### Where it happens (main @ dd250e6)

### Use Case

https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight-php

A community PHP client for the Hindsight API, with long-term memory for agents built on the official [Laravel AI SDK](https://github.com/laravel/ai) (`laravel/ai`). I'd like it listed in the Integrations Hub as a community integration.

```php
class SupportAgent implements Agent, HasMiddleware
{
    use Promptable;

    public function middleware(): array
    {
        return [Memory::bank("user-{$this->user->id}")];
    }
}
```

The `Memory` middleware recalls relevant memories before the agent's first generation step and retains the exchange after the step that ends the run. `Recall`, `Retain` and `Reflect` tools are there for agents that should decide for themselves.

### Problem Statement

There are official clients for Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust, but nothing for PHP, so Laravel developers write raw HTTP calls.

### How This Feature Would Help

A listing in the hub lets PHP and Laravel developers find a tested client instead of starting from scratch.

### Proposed Solution

An entry in `hindsight-docs/src/data/integrations.json`, for example:

```json
{
  "id": "hindsight-php",
  "name": "PHP & Laravel AI SDK",
  "description": "PHP client for the Hindsight API, plus long-term memory middleware and recall/retain/reflect tools for Laravel AI SDK agents.",
  "type": "community",
  "by": "skybleak333",
  "category": "framework",
  "link": "https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight-php"
}
```

For the icon, a PHP or Laravel logo would fit; I can provide one if needed.

### Priority

Nice to have

### Additional Context

- Client: retain (single, batch, async), recall, reflect, banks and bank config, memories, documents, directives, mental models, operations with `waitForOperation()`, and `request()` for anything else. Method names follow the Python and TypeScript clients.
- It reads the `X-Ignored-Params` response header and turns it into a PSR-3 warning, so a misspelled option shows up instead of silently changing results.
- Testing: every request in the unit tests is validated against the 1.1.0 OpenAPI document (stricter than the server: unknown fields fail). CI runs the integration suite against a real `hindsight-api-slim==1.1.0` server with `LLM_PROVIDER=none`, on PHP 8.2–8.5, Laravel 12 and 13, Laravel AI SDK 1.0 and 1.3, and the lowest allowed dependencies.

The entry is ready as a commit in my fork, in the same shape as the one in #5842: [717e14e](https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/717e14e76b6a74feb10e96f455a77034b6051979) adds it to `integrations.json` and adds a PHP icon (`static/img/icons/php.svg`). It is based on today's `main`.

issue.title: Malformed input answers 500 instead of 4xx: non-UUID directive ids, out-of-range directive priority, NUL bytes outside retain
issue.body:
### Bug Description

Several requests with ordinary client mistakes reach Postgres and come back as `500`, while the same kind of mistake elsewhere in the API already gets a `4xx`. A client, or an SDK that retries on 5xx, cannot tell them apart from a server fault.

I sent edge-case requests to a fresh local server (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`). 10 of 130 answered `500`, in three groups:

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET` / `PATCH` / `DELETE /directives/not-a-uuid` | `500 invalid input for query argument $2: 'not-a-uuid' (invalid UUID ...)` |
| `DELETE /memories/not-a-uuid/observations` | `500 badly formed hexadecimal UUID string` |
| `POST /directives` with `"priority": 2147483648` | `500 ... value out of int32 range` |
| NUL byte (`\u0000`) in a recall `tags` filter | `500 Failed to search memories (CharacterNotInRepertoireError)` |
| NUL byte in `GET /memories/list?q=` | `500 invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00` |
| NUL byte in a document id (`GET /documents/a%00b`) | same |
| NUL byte in a directive name or content | same |
| NUL byte in a bank `name` (`PUT /banks/{id}`) | same |

For comparison, `GET /memories/not-a-uuid` already answers `400 Invalid memory_id: 'not-a-uuid' is not a valid UUID` (#3062), and retain scrubs NUL bytes (#3908, #3921).

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
pip install "hindsight-api-slim[local-onnx,embedded-db]==1.1.0"
HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=onnx HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_PROVIDER=rrf hindsight-api

B=http://localhost:8888/v1/default/banks/demo
J='Content-Type: application/json'
curl -s -X POST "$B/memories" -H "$J" -d '{"items":[{"content":"Alice works at Google."}]}'

curl -s "$B/directives/not-a-uuid"
curl -s -X DELETE "$B/memories/not-a-uuid/observations"
curl -s -X POST "$B/directives" -H "$J" -d '{"name":"n","content":"c","priority":2147483648}'
curl -s -X POST "$B/memories/recall" -H "$J" -d '{"query":"alice","tags":["a\u0000"]}'
curl -s "$B/memories/list?q=a%00b"
```

### Expected Behavior

A `4xx` that names the problem, like the routes that already validate their input.

### Actual Behavior

`500`, with the database error as the detail, and an `ERROR` traceback in the server log for each request.

### Where it happens (main @ dd250e6)

- `MemoryEngine.get_directive`, `update_directive` and `delete_directive` pass `directive_id` straight to the query. `clear_observations_for_memory` calls `uuid.UUID(memory_id)` inside the transaction. None of the four routes catch `ValueError`.
- `CreateDirectiveRequest.priority` and `UpdateDirectiveRequest.priority` are unbounded `int`, but `directives.priority` is `INT`.
- `_internal_error`, and the recall, retain and reflect-tool catch-alls, map every database error to `500`, including SQLSTATE `22021` (character_not_in_repertoire) and `22P05` (untranslatable_character). On these routes that text always comes from the client.

### Patch

CONTRIBUTING says external PRs are closed, so the fix is on a fork branch you can cherry-pick or rewrite: https://github.com/skybleak333/hindsight/commit/bea0cb7883c4b901b552108b65975914eced81dc (6 files, +328/−4)

- The four routes raise and map the same `Invalid ...: '...' is not a valid UUID` `ValueError` to `400`, like #3062, and pass the canonical id on. Otherwise `{...}` and `urn:uuid:...` spellings, which `uuid.UUID` accepts and the uuid column rejects, would still 500; now they get the usual `404`.
- A shared `check_directive_priority()` runs as a field validator on the two request models and on `BankTemplateDirective`, and in `create_directive` / `update_directive` for the MCP tools. A template import with an out-of-range priority now fails before it writes anything. I used validators instead of `ge`/`le` so the OpenAPI and bank-template schemas, and the generated clients, stay unchanged.
- A small `_unstorable_text()` helper walks the cause chain like `_store_unavailable()` and maps those two SQLSTATEs to `400`. `_internal_error` and the three custom catch-alls use it.
- Tests: stub-engine tests for the id checks and canonical forms (same pattern as `test_get_entity_uuid_validation.py`), priority tests for the models and the engine, `_internal_error` tests, and a structural test that every catch-all calling `_store_unavailable` by hand also calls `_unstorable_text`. The new tests fail on `dd250e6`.

Not covered: a lone surrogate (`\ud800`) in the same fields still answers `500`, because asyncpg fails to encode it before the query is sent. That probably needs a separate decision on where to reject it.

With the patch, the same 130 requests produce no `5xx`. `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

### Version

1.1.0 (`hindsight-api-slim` from PyPI), and main @ dd250e6

### LLM Provider

None (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER=none`); not involved.

issue.title: non_blocking=true in Consumer::daemon() silently defeats heartbeat-based dead-connection detection
issue.body:
`Consumer::daemon()` always calls:

```php
$this->channel->wait(null, true, (int) $options->timeout);
```

The true (non_blocking) makes AbstractChannel::wait() throw $timeout away and set it to null before it ever reaches the socket, so --timeout has zero effect on this call (it still works for the per-job pcntl_alarm watchdog elsewhere in the same file — same option, two unrelated meanings, which is its own confusion but not the main point).

The real issue is heartbeat. In non-blocking mode the library throws AMQPNoDataException on every empty poll instead of AMQPTimeoutException — and the only code that actually compares "when did I last hear from the broker" (last_frame) against heartbeat lives inside catch (AMQPTimeoutException) in wait_channel(). That block never runs. There's a second heartbeat check in AbstractIO::select() that does run regardless of blocking mode, but it keys off max(last_read, last_write) — and a local fwrite() succeeding (accepted into the kernel send buffer) counts as "activity" whether or not the broker ever actually got the bytes. So neither path catches a silently dead socket.

Easy to reproduce: set heartbeat=15, get a worker consuming, then freeze the broker (kill -STOP on the process, or just black-hole the port so no FIN/RST ever arrives). The worker keeps polling forever — zero errors, zero reconnect — heartbeat config or not.

This was already raised in #296 back in 2020, closed with "blocking mode is not a solution because timeouts will not work," which mixes up this wait() timeout with the unrelated --timeout/pcntl_alarm one — a different commenter on that thread pointed out the same mixup at the time.

There's also #414, still open, proposing the same switch as an opt-in flag. That thread stalled on whether the latency win is worth it, since it was pitched purely as a perf improvement - a fair question, but a different one from this issue. This isn't about speed, it's that heartbeat doesn't function at all, at any value, while non_blocking=true. Worth noting #414 also passes $options->timeout straight through to wait() instead of a separate value - with the default --timeout=60 that makes daemonShouldRun()/pause checks up to 20x less responsive, which may be what "not all features worked" (the maintainer's reply there, never elaborated on) was actually about.

For what it's worth, #632 independently ran into the same symptom from production and describes it almost word for word: "the consumer works, RabbitMQ sees the consumer, but messages don't reach the consumer at all... happens with a complex architecture with virtual machines and/or proxies." Its fix is a separate active RPC probe (alive-check), not heartbeat, and only applies to the new opt-in blocking mode - doesn't touch the default path this issue is about - but it's a useful independent confirmation that this isn't a one-off local reproduction.

The CPU concern behind non_blocking doesn't apply to a real blocking select() either — checked it locally, it just sleeps in the kernel (poll_schedule_timeout), 0% CPU.

Minimal fix: wait(null, false, $waitTimeout) with its own short timeout, separate from $options->timeout (already spoken for by the job watchdog), plus a no-op catch (AMQPTimeoutException) next to the existing AMQPNoDataException swallow. That alone makes heartbeat do what the config implies.

(tested against v3.4.0/v12.0.1, but the wait() call hasn't changed since the very first commit that introduced it in 2019)

comment.body:
Reproduced on current `master` (92ebf07) plus #680, with Laravel 13.37, php-amqplib 3.7.5, RabbitMQ 3.13.3 and heartbeat 15 s. With the broker frozen (`docker compose pause`), an idle `rabbitmq:consume` reports nothing for the whole 100 s. This runs in CI as experiment 2 of https://github.com/skybleak333/laravel-queue-lab.

The cause is the one described here. The non-blocking `wait()` never times out, so `wait_channel()` never checks the age of the last frame. The other check, `AbstractIO::checkBrokerHeartbeat()`, counts the client's own heartbeat writes. php-amqplib#1227 is about that second check; I posted measurements there: https://github.com/php-amqplib/php-amqplib/issues/1227#issuecomment-6239409018

Heartbeats plus a `channel_rpc_timeout` of 10 s, with read and write timeouts raised to match, make it stop with `LostConnection` 42 s after the freeze.

issue.title: use blocking wait() with its own timeout instead of non_blocking
issue.body:
Fixes #673

non_blocking=true is what breaks heartbeat detection - AbstractChannel::wait() forces the timeout to null, the library throws AMQPNoDataException instead of AMQPTimeoutException on every empty poll, and the last_frame-vs-heartbeat check that only runs inside a caught AMQPTimeoutException never gets a chance to fire.

This switches to a real blocking wait() with its own --wait-timeout, kept separate from --timeout since that option already does something unrelated (per-job pcntl_alarm watchdog). Added a no-op catch for the resulting AMQPTimeoutException on ordinary empty polls - same as AMQPNoDataException was silently swallowed before, just one level up. Dropped the sleep() that used to run after every empty wait() cycle, since the blocking wait already paces the loop; keeping it would've just added --sleep on top of --wait-timeout for no reason.

This is a behavior change, not additive: non_blocking flips from true to false by default. Happy to gate it behind a flag instead if you'd rather ship it opt-in.

Tested against v3.4.0/v12.0.1 to confirm the bug, then rebased onto current master.

issue.title: Worker silently stops consuming after PRECONDITION_FAILED (406) channel exception in pop()

comment.body:
I tried to reproduce this with RabbitMQ 3.13.3 and `consumer_timeout = 60000`, PHP 8.4 and php-amqplib 3.7.5:

- package v14.1.0 and v14.4.0 on Laravel 11.51 (v14.0–v14.4 don't boot on 11.52+ because of the `Consumer::stop()` signature);
- `63e5c37` (tag v14.5.3) on Laravel 11.52;
- current `master` with the fix from #680 on Laravel 11.57 and 13.36.

The scenario was one job that sleeps 150 s (A), then two quick jobs (B and C) on the same queue. The broker closed the channel 60–120 s after A was delivered.

I couldn't reproduce the hang. In every combination the worker exited:

- `queue:work`: after A finished, the next `pop()` got the 406 `PRECONDITION_FAILED`, the following `pop()` got `Lost connection: Channel connection is closed.`, and the worker stopped with exit code 0 (reason `LostConnection` on Laravel 11.52+).
- `rabbitmq:consume`: the 406 comes from `wait()` in `Consumer`, not from `pop()`. php-amqplib clears the channel callbacks, the `is_consuming()` loop ends, and the process exits with code 0 without `WorkerStopping`.

What does go wrong is redelivery. The ack sent when A finishes goes to a channel the broker has already closed, so A runs a second time. With `rabbitmq:consume` and the default prefetch, B and C had already been delivered to the client: the worker ran them after the broker had put them back in the queue, so they ran twice as well. With `--prefetch-count=1` only A ran twice.

The proposed `pop()` change (I applied it temporarily) stops `queue:work` one loop earlier, about 2 s in my run, but A still runs twice, and `rabbitmq:consume` behaves the same. Keeping `consumer_timeout` above the longest job avoids the redelivery; since RabbitMQ 3.12 it can be set per queue with the `x-consumer-timeout` argument or the `consumer-timeout` policy.

Both commands exit with code 0 here, so supervisord with its default `autorestart=unexpected` won't restart them; `autorestart=true`, as in the Laravel docs, will.

First experiment: what `queue:work` and `rabbitmq:consume` do when a job outlives RabbitMQ's delivery acknowledgement timeout.

- Both commands exit with code 0 after the 406 instead of hanging.
- The slow job runs twice. With `rabbitmq:consume` and the default prefetch, the jobs already in the client buffer run twice as well.

Checked in CI with PHP 8.3–8.5, Laravel 13.37, php-amqplib 3.7.5 and RabbitMQ 3.13.3. Until vyuldashev/laravel-queue-rabbitmq#680 is released, the package is installed from its branch.
